fields.included: Whole-report lexical scope reconciled across all 124 PDF pages: Appendix E, printed pages 75--118, contributes 1,438 manually transcribed lexical variants from 1,401 responsive cells; Appendix B.1--B.7, printed pages 17--31, contributes 205 narrative/question units and five explicitly named terms; section 3.1.4, printed pages 6--7, contributes 18 comparative attestations. Total 1,666 source rows across seven Koya, Gondi and Madia lects. Sixty-nine missing wordlist target slots, 420 Telugu/Oriya wordlist controls, Telugu test narratives, English questionnaires, numeric scores, a festival name without lexical definition, and documentary matter remain accounted for outside target output

fields.note: Survey fieldwork 1985--1986. Seven lects retain canonical Gondi and their registered locality tags. Narrative spelling is preserved without invented phonemic interpretation; section3.1.4 G maps to voiced velar fricative following its explicit definition. Wordlists retain their separate phonetic profile. Source free translations remain paired at printed segment boundaries, without inferred word alignment. Expected comprehension answers are audit evidence rather than lexical gloss content. Explicitly named but undefined terms retain blank glosses and context. No cognate edges inferred from sound comparisons. Existing wordlist uncertainty remains in audit and tags; no new coordinates inferred
